note: Gates the gate: it MUST return verified-good on a load-bearing suite, verified-bad on a decorative one, UNVERIFIABLE when a mutant dies unobserved, UNVERIFIABLE on an empty inventory, and it MUST execute the bytes it wrote rather than a previous mutant's cached bytecode. `check` READS this file — inverting any expectation here reds the suite.

vectors.name: crashing
vectors.note: CRASH != KILLED. A mutant that dies without the declared kill_witness was not observed by any assertion. Regression control for bin/recompute-mutation-survival:73.

vectors.name: stale-bytecode
vectors.note: EXECUTION FRESHNESS control. Both mutants are same-byte-length edits to one file, so the source size never changes; the test command additionally stamps a fixed mtime, so mtime cannot discriminate either. CPython validates timestamp .pyc on (mtime, size), so without per-run isolation every run reuses the baseline's bytecode and BOTH mutants are misread. Pinning both rows is deliberate: pinning only the survivor would let a run that got the first mutant wrong still pass. Remove the Workspace isolation and this vector reds. (zexoverz, 2026-10-12.)

vectors.name: zero-mutants
vectors.note: An empty inventory certified coverage: killed 0 / survived 0 read as verified-good / exit 0. Same class as #65 ZERO_MUTANTS, but it has to be guarded at this tool's own boundary because #66 discovers suites by mutation_check.py and this suite has none. Remove the guard and this vector reds. (zexoverz, 2026-10-12.)
